title: Sharp rank-three Chollet inequalities in order five
oneLine: An exact rational certificate proves the sharp order-five rank-three permanent inequality, classifies equality, and yields the sharp two-matrix form.
abstract: For every real 5 by 5 correlation matrix C of rank at most three, this computer-assisted mathematical candidate proves per(C circle C) at most 13/48 times per(C) squared, with equality exactly at signed simultaneous permutations of J2 direct-sum E3. It also proves the sharp mixed inequality per(A circle B) at most 13/48 per(A)per(B) for real positive-semidefinite rank-at-most-three matrices and classifies all equality cases. The proof combines a written Gram reduction with a symmetry-adapted rational sum-of-squares certificate and exact standard-library replay. The certificate-construction pipeline is unavailable, and no external specialist review or formal verification is claimed.

narration: The sharp rank 3 constant. An Evidence Press briefing. A matrix permanent looks like a determinant with every sign made positive. That makes it useful, and notoriously difficult to control. This paper studies a precise 5x5, rank 3 case of a permanent inequality associated with Chollet. Start with a real correlation matrix C. Square each entry to form the Hadamard product C circle C. The candidate proves that its permanent is at most 13 over 48 times the square of the permanent of C. The constant is sharp. Equality has one exact geometry: after reordering the five indices and switching compatible signs, two indices form an all-ones block, while the other three form an equiangular block with off-diagonal entries minus one half. At this witness, the separate permanent equals 3. The squared-entry permanent equals 39 over 16. Their ratio is exactly 13 over 48. Review also produced a stronger two-matrix statement. For real positive-semidefinite 5x5 matrices A and B, each of rank at most 3, the permanent of A circle B obeys the same sharp constant times the two separate permanents. Equality requires a common 2-plus-3 partition, apart from degenerate zero-row cases. The proof is computer-assisted but exact. A rational sum-of-squares certificate and a standard-library checker expand the full polynomial identity. The remainder is built from 4x4 Gram determinants, which vanish at rank 3. Corruption tests reject three proof-relevant changes, and a separate implementation reproduced the decisive finite calculations. Important limits remain. The original certificate generator and repair trace are unavailable, so the package checks but does not regenerate the certificate. The written reduction still needs mathematical scrutiny. This is a real, order 5, rank at most 3 result, not the unrestricted Chollet conjecture. It is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, without external specialist review or proof-assistant formalisation. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
